fields.name: Chair Yoga and Tea Time with Ksenya
fields.preview:
Dear Nordic Walkers and Friends ,
I warmly invite you to join us for gentle re-strenghening, re-balancing, and inner warmth during the cold winter season.
Winter naturally slows us down and our joints feel stiffer, muscles tighten, circulation becomes sluggish, and we often carry extra tension in the shoulders, hips, and lower back. Chair Yoga is a beautiful antidote, helping us soften, restore mobility, and reconnect with breath and ease when the body needs it most.
What to bring:
• The thinnest long bath towel (or a long pillowcase or yoga strap)
• Your favorite mug for tea
• Warm socks (optional, but super comfortable and cozy!)
• A smile (a must!)
What to wear: Comfortable clothing
Suitable for: All ages and fitness levels
$5 per class (as a personal donation)
After class, please stay and enjoy a cup of Ksenya’s Balancing Herbal Tea — a soothing blend to gently refresh the body and lift the spirit.
Why Chair Yoga?
Chair Yoga is a gentle yet powerful practice that restores balance, flexibility, and inner calm.
• For Nordic Walkers, it’s the perfect complement — easing tight joints and muscles, strengthening the core, improving posture, and enhancing breathing after energizing walks.
• For everyone else, it offers a safe and nurturing way to release tension, improve circulation, calm the nervous system, and find joy in movement - all from the comfort of a chair.
Let’s stretch, breathe, warm up, and rejuvenate together!
See you every Tuesday at the John Curtis Free Library!
With warmth and joy,
Ksenya

fields.content:
Nordic Walking United

If you are to learn how to do Nordic Walking, we have good news for you: we are holding XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX for beginners!

It will take place on DAY, MONTH, YEAR at VENUE in CITY.

We believe the IT industry will greatly benefit from bringing more women into technology. We want to give you an opportunity to learn how to program and become one of us – women programmers!

Workshops are free of charge and if you cannot afford coming to CITY but are very motivated to learn and then share your knowledge with others, we may have some funds to help you out with your travel costs and accommodation. Don't wait too long: you can apply for the workshop only until DATE!

Apply for the workshop!

If you are a woman, know English and have a laptop, you can apply for our event! You don't need to know any technical stuff – our workshop is for people who are new to programming.

As a workshop attendee you will:

  • attend a one-day Django workshop during which you will create your first website
  • be fed by us: during our event, food is provided

We have space only for XX people, so make sure to fill out the form very carefully!

fields.name: apply
fields.content:
Applications are now open!

Register

fields.name: faq
fields.content:
Do I need to know anything about websites or programming?

No! Workshops are for beginners. You don’t need to know anything about it. However, if you have a little bit of technical knowledge (i.e. you know what HTML or CSS are) you still can apply!

I am not living in Germany, can I attend?

Of course! Workshops will be in English, so if you have no troubles with speaking and understanding English - you should apply. If you need financial aid to get to Berlin or you need assistance with booking flights or hotel in Berlin - let us know. We are willing to help you!

Should I bring my own laptop?

Yes. We have no hardware, so we expect you to bring your computer with you. It is also important for us that you will take home everything you’ll write and create during workshops.

Do I need to have something installed on my laptop?

It would be helpful to have Django installed before workshops, but wouldn't expect you to install anything on your own.We will make sure that one of our coaches will help you out with this task.

Is EuroPython conference good for a total beginner?

As a workshop attendee you will get a free ticket to EuroPython - conference for Python programmers. Even though you are new to programming,conference is a good place to meet many interesting people in the industry and find inspiration.

Is food provided?

Yes. Thanks to EuroPython, snacks and lunch will be served during workshops.

This workshop is a part of bigger initiative: Django Girls. It is a non-profit organization and events are organized by volunteers in different places of the world.

To see the source for the program find us on Github: github.com/DjangoGirls.

fields.title: Register for Your First Event
fields.body:
Welcome to Nordic Walking United - we’re excited to have you join us on this journey!

Here’s a simple guide to help you sign up for your very first event:

Browse Our Events

To see what’s coming up, click Quick Links in the top menu. From the drop-down list, select EVENTS to view all upcoming walks and activities.

Pick What Inspires You

Scroll through the events and choose the walk or activity that feels right for you. Each one is an opportunity to move, connect, and enjoy the outdoors together.

Tip: You can sort events by country and city, too!

 Begin Registration

 Once you’ve chosen your event, look to the top-right corner of the event page and click the green REGISTER button.

Review and Accept Our Policies

Please please review the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and Photo & Media Release by clicking each tab, then check the box confirming your acceptance and click the green “I Agree & Continue to Registration” button to proceed.

Add your information.

Fill in your basic personal details and enter your email and password - these will be your keys to all future NWU events. Please remember or save them for next time. Click the green “Register” button when you’re ready.

Confirm Your Spot

After registering, review the event details and click the SIGNUP button to officially secure your place.

Logging In Next Time

Now that you’re part of the NWU family, signing up again is easy! Simply choose the event you’d like to attend, click LOGIN in the top menu, enter your username and password, and you’re ready to go.

See you on the trails soon! 🌿

fields.title: Apply to Organize a Nordic Walking Group
fields.table_title: How to apply to organize a NWU group
fields.body:
1. Getting Started 🌿

We’re so happy you’re here and interested in bringing Nordic Walking to your community. This guide will walk you step by step through starting a new group or registering an existing Nordic Walking group within our NWU community.

You can begin in two easy ways:

  • Option 1: On the main page, click the green “Organize a New Nordic Walking Group” button.
  • Option 2: From the top menu, choose Quick Links → Organize a Nordic Walking Group.

Both options will take you to the same multi-step application form.

 

2. Prerequisites to Organize a Nordic Walking Group

You are now on the “Prerequisites to Organize a Nordic Walking Group” page.

To continue, please take a moment to read all required documents:

  • Click each green link next to the checkboxes to open a document.
  • Each document will open in a new browser tab.
  • After reading a document and agreeing with its contents, return to the previous tab and check the corresponding box.

Once all documents are read and all checkboxes are checked, click the green “Get Started” button to move forward.

Each document will open in a new browser tab:

3. Organizer Commitment 🌱

Welcome to the Nordic Walking Group Organizer Commitment page!

Please click the link to read the Nordic Walking United Code of Conduct.

  • The document will open in a separate tab.

  • After reading and agreeing with it, return to the original tab and click the green “Sign the Commitment” button to continue.

4. Application to Start a New Nordic Walking Group

On this page, you’ll be asked whether you have previously organized a Nordic Walking group within the NWU community.

  • Select “Yes” if you have organized a group with us before - the system will skip ahead to Step 6, since we already have most of your details.
  • Select “No” if this is your first time - you’ll continue to Step 5 to tell us more about yourself and your motivation.

When ready, click “Go to Next Step.”

5. Application for First-Time Organizers

(This step will be skipped if you have organized a group with NWU before.)

This section helps us learn more about you and your motivation for organizing a Nordic Walking group.

Please be honest and descriptive - the more you share, the better we can understand your vision, and the smoother the approval process will be.

All fields are required.

When finished, click “Go to Next Step.”

6. Who Will Be Organizing This Nordic Walking Group?

This page helps us understand who will manage your group and events.

The first section is for the Lead Organizer - that’s you!
Please enter your first name, last name, and email (all fields are required).

Below that, you may add Your organizing team (Moderators) who will help manage your group and events.
Moderators can create, edit, and delete events within your group.

To add more organizers, click the “+ ” button.

fields.title: Nordic Walking in Clinical Trials and Findings
fields.body:
🏃‍♀️ Nordic Walking in the United States

Nordic walking is a full-body exercise using poles to engage both the upper and lower body. Originating in Finland, it has become popular in the United States for fitness, rehabilitation, and wellness. The technique emphasizes posture, rhythm, and coordinated movement, offering a low-impact yet highly effective workout.

🇺🇸 U.S. Organizations Promoting Nordic Walking

  • American Nordic Walking Association (ANWA) – Provides instructor certifications, workshops, and community events.
  • INWA USA – The official U.S. branch of the International Nordic Walking Federation, promoting standardized techniques and education.
  • Local health and recreation programs – Many local clubs, YMCAs, and wellness centers include Nordic walking in rehabilitation and fitness programs.

🧬 Relationship with Clinical Trials

While Nordic walking organizations focus on training and community health, clinical trials are generally conducted by universities, hospitals, and research institutions. These studies explore its effects on cardiovascular health, neurological conditions, and musculoskeletal function.

🧪 Key U.S. Clinical Trials and Findings

1️⃣ Cardiovascular and Metabolic Health

Institution: University of Wisconsin–La Crosse
Findings: Nordic walking improved aerobic capacity (VO₂ max) and reduced blood pressure compared with regular walking, with participants reporting greater enjoyment and adherence.

2️⃣ Parkinson’s Disease

Institution: Cleveland Clinic, Ohio
Findings: Improved gait speed, stride length, and balance; reduced fall risk and improved quality of life.

3️⃣ Osteoarthritis and Joint Health

Institution: University of Pittsburgh
Findings: Reduced joint loading and pain, improved mobility, and better adherence compared with traditional walking programs.

4️⃣ Obesity and Diabetes

Institution: Mayo Clinic, Minnesota
Findings: Enhanced insulin sensitivity, reduced body fat, and higher energy expenditure than standard walking.

5️⃣ Multiple Sclerosis (MS)

Institution: University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus
Findings: Improved balance, endurance, and fatigue levels; participants reported greater confidence and mobility.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Correct Length & Adjusting Nordic Walking Poles
fields.body:
Follow these simple steps to set your Nordic Walking poles for comfort, posture, and effective support:

  1. Determine the Correct Length

    Hold the pole upside down and grip it just below the basket or tip. Your elbow should form a 90° angle, and your forearm should be parallel to the ground. If so, the length is correct.

  2. Loosen the Locking Mechanism

    Poles may have different types of locks such as twist locks, flip locks, or lever locks. Locate and loosen the mechanism just enough to allow adjustment.

  3. Adjust the Length

    Extend or shorten each pole to reach your desired length. Use the markings (if available) to ensure both poles are the same length.

  4. Secure the Locking Mechanism

    Tighten the locking mechanism firmly according to the manufacturer’s instructions. It should hold securely without slipping.

  5. Test the Adjustment

    Hold the poles correctly, keeping your wrist aligned with the pole and your hand comfortably wrapped around the handle. Take a few steps and check your posture and comfort. Adjust again if necessary.

Remember: Always adjust both poles to the same length and check that the locks remain secure during your walk.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Correct Use of the Regular (Basic) Pole Strap
fields.body:
Proper strap technique lets you relax your grip, transfer power efficiently, and keep a smooth rhythm. Follow the steps below to fit and use your straps.

  1. Proper Hand Placement
    Insert your hand from underneath the strap so it lies across the back of your hand. The adjustment buckle should face outward (away from your palm).
  2. Slide Your Hand In
    Feed your hand deeper into the strap until it rests across the base of your fingers and the back of your hand. Adjust so it’s snug but not tight.
  3. Create a Support Loop
    With your hand in the strap, form a natural loop by letting your thumb rest against the strap on the palm side. This loop helps keep your hand secure and prevents slipping during your swing.
  4. Maintain a Relaxed Grip
    Walk with a light, relaxed hold on the handle—avoid clenching. Let the strap carry the load as you push back, then briefly open your hand during the back swing and re-grip as the pole comes forward.

Why it matters

Straps add support and stability, improving power transfer and reducing hand fatigue. Correct strap use promotes a more natural, efficient technique and a better overall experience.

Quick tips

  • Right strap on right hand, left strap on left hand (they’re often labeled “R” and “L”).
  • If your fingers tingle or the strap rubs, loosen and re-adjust.
  • Keep the buckle flat and off your skin to avoid chafing.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Warm-Up Exercises Before Nordic Walking
fields.body:
Before starting your Nordic Walking session, take 3–5 minutes to warm up your muscles and joints. Perform each exercise for 20–30 seconds per side (where applicable) with smooth, controlled motion.

  1. Neck Rotations

    Stand tall. Gently rotate your head in a slow circle clockwise, then counterclockwise. Keep shoulders relaxed.

  2. Arm Circles

    Feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended at shoulder height. Make small circles, gradually increasing the size. Reverse direction halfway.

  3. Shoulder Rolls

    Lift shoulders toward ears, roll back and down. Repeat, then switch to forward rolls.

  4. Torso Twists

    Feet hip-width apart, soft knees. Gently twist your upper body side-to-side, letting arms swing loosely.

  5. Hip Circles

    Hands on hips. Draw wide circles with your hips clockwise, then counterclockwise to mobilize the hip joints.

  6. Knee Lifts (March in Place)

    March in place, lifting knees toward chest. Keep posture tall and engage your core.

  7. Ankle Rotations

    Standing or seated, lift one foot and rotate the ankle both directions. Switch sides.

  8. Calf Stretch

    Step one foot back, heel down, knee straight. Lean forward to stretch the back calf. Switch sides.

  9. Hamstring Stretch

    Extend one leg forward with heel on the ground and toes up. Hinge slightly at the hips, keeping back long. Switch sides.

  10. Quad Stretch

    Stand tall (hold a pole or wall for balance). Bend one knee and draw heel toward glutes, knees together. Switch sides.

Tips

  • Breathe naturally—never hold your breath.
  • Move within a comfortable, pain-free range.
  • Use your poles or a wall for balance as needed.
  • Here is a helpful video you can watch and follow at your own pace: 
    ▶ See how to stretch on YouTube

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Cool Down Exercises After Nordic Walking
fields.body:
Cooling down after Nordic Walking is important to gradually reduce your heart rate, relax your muscles, and prevent stiffness. Here are ten cool-down exercises you can incorporate:

  1. Slow Walking: After your walk, gradually slow down your pace. Continue walking at a slower speed for a few minutes to ease your heart rate back to its normal range.
  2. Hamstring Stretch: Stand with one foot in front of the other and gently lean forward, keeping your back straight, to stretch your hamstrings.
  3. Calf Stretch: Stand facing a wall or tree, place one foot behind you, and press your heel into the ground to stretch your calf muscles.
  4. Quad Stretch: Stand on one leg and gently pull your other heel toward your buttocks to stretch your quadriceps.
  5. Hip Flexor Stretch: Step one foot behind you, bend your front knee, and gently push your hips forward to stretch your hip flexors.
  6. Trunk Rotation: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and slowly twist your torso to one side and then the other to relax your spine.
  7. Shoulder Rolls: Roll your shoulders forward and backward to release tension in your shoulders and upper back.
  8. Neck Stretches: Gently tilt your head to one side and hold for a few seconds, then switch to the other side to release tension in your neck.
  9. Deep Breathing: Take a few minutes to practice deep, calming breaths. Inhale deeply through your nose, hold for a few seconds, and exhale slowly through your mouth.
  10. Hydration and Nutrition: Drink water and, if needed, have a light, healthy snack to replenish your energy and support recovery.

Perform each cool-down exercise for about 20–30 seconds, focusing on deep breathing and relaxation. Cooling down helps your body recover and reduces post-exercise soreness.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Correct Nordic Walking Posture
fields.body:
Proper posture is essential for safe, efficient, and enjoyable Nordic Walking. Use these key points as a gentle checklist while you walk:

  1. Stand Tall: Stand up straight with your head held high and your eyes looking forward. Imagine a string gently pulling you up from the top of your head to lengthen your spine. Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid slouching or rounding your back.
  2. Engage Core Muscles: Gently draw your navel toward your spine to activate your core muscles. This helps stabilize your torso and maintain proper alignment. Keep your abdominal muscles lightly engaged without holding your breath or tensing too much.
  3. Maintain a Neutral Pelvis: Position your pelvis in a neutral alignment — not tilted too far forward or backward. Imagine a bowl of water resting on your pelvis and try to keep it level. This posture supports stability and even weight distribution.
  4. Forward Arm Swing: Coordinate your arm swing with your steps: when your right foot steps forward, your left arm (with the pole) swings forward, and vice versa. Keep the movement relaxed, natural, and fluid — avoid stiff or exaggerated motions.

  5. Land Midfoot and Roll Through: Aim to land gently on your heel, then smoothly roll through the midfoot to your toes. This promotes efficient, balanced walking and reduces impact. Avoid heavy heel strikes or walking only on your toes.

Regularly check in with your posture during Nordic Walking and adjust as needed. A comfortable, aligned posture improves stability, efficiency, and overall enjoyment.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Breathing While Nordic Walking
fields.body:
Breathing well during Nordic Walking helps maintain stamina, provides oxygen to your muscles, and promotes relaxation. Use these tips to develop an effective and comfortable breathing pattern:

  1. Breathe Naturally: Allow your breath to flow in a relaxed, natural way. Avoid forcing or over-controlling your breathing. Keep it easy and rhythmic.
  2. Use Diaphragmatic (Belly) Breathing: Focus on deep breathing into your abdomen rather than shallow chest breathing. As you inhale, let your belly gently expand; as you exhale, let it soften and contract naturally.
  3. Coordinate Breathing with Movement: Sync your breath with your arm and leg movements to create a smooth rhythm. For example, inhale over a few steps as one arm swings forward, and exhale over the next few steps as the opposite arm swings forward. Find a pattern that feels natural and supports your pace.
  4. Maintain a Steady Pace: Aim for steady, even breaths instead of rapid or shallow breathing. Adjust your breathing rhythm to match your walking speed and effort level so you can sustain a comfortable, continuous walk.
  5. Practice Relaxation and Mindfulness: Use your breathing to release tension and calm your mind. Notice each inhale and exhale, and let go of stress with every out-breath. Stay present, relaxed, and enjoy the movement and nature around you.

Everyone’s breathing pattern is slightly different, so listen to your body and choose what feels best. If you feel short of breath or fatigued, slow down or pause to recover. With practice, your breathing will become naturally efficient and supportive of your Nordic Walking.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Nordic Walking Pole’s Tips
fields.body:
Nordic Walking poles come with different types of tips, each designed for specific terrains and conditions. Choosing the right tip helps improve stability, comfort, and efficiency during your walks.

  • Power Snow Baskets: Ideal for terrains with powdery snow, providing extra support and preventing the poles from sinking too deeply.
  • Snow Baskets: Best for thick snow conditions, offering wider surface contact to keep poles stable.
  • Mud Baskets: Suitable for soft or muddy ground such as beaches, wetlands, or swampy areas. They prevent poles from going too deep into the ground.
  • Rubber Tips: Universal tips that work well on most terrains, including gravel, dirt paths, and indoor surfaces. They also reduce noise and protect the metal tip.

  • Asphalt Paws: Designed for hard surfaces such as asphalt or paved trails. Their angled rubber design provides excellent grip and shock absorption.

The choice of tip depends on the terrain you plan to walk on, so it’s a good idea to keep a variety of tips on hand if you enjoy walking in different environments. Always make sure your tips are securely attached to your poles to prevent accidents or damage.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: The Major Benefits of Nordic Walking
fields.body:
Nordic Walking is more than just walking with poles — it’s a fun, effective, and holistic form of exercise that benefits the body and mind. Here are some of its key advantages:

  • Enjoyable: Anyone can be good at it! Nordic Walking is easy to learn and enjoyable for people of all ages and fitness levels.
  • Adventure: Discover new and beautiful places in the South Shore and beyond while staying active outdoors.
  • Full-Body Workout: Engages multiple muscle groups — including arms, shoulders, core, and legs — for a balanced, whole-body workout.
  • Cardiovascular Fitness: Improves heart health and increases aerobic capacity through sustained rhythmic movement.
  • Weight Management: Helps with weight loss and maintenance by increasing calorie burn during every walk.
  • Balance and Coordination: Enhances stability and coordination through the active use of poles.
  • Posture Improvement: Encourages an upright posture and reduces spinal strain.
  • Enhanced Endurance: Builds stamina and endurance, allowing for longer, more enjoyable walks with less fatigue.
  • Stress Reduction: The natural rhythm and outdoor environment help calm the mind and reduce stress.
  • Improved Mood: Boosts endorphin levels, improving mood and reducing symptoms of anxiety or depression.
  • Bone Health: Helps maintain bone density and lowers the risk of osteoporosis.
  • Enhanced Upper Body Strength: Strengthens arms, shoulders, and back muscles, helping to ease neck and shoulder tension.
  • Accessible: Can be practiced almost anywhere — from city parks to beaches, trails, and quiet neighborhoods.
  • Social Interaction: A great way to connect with others and make new friends when walking in groups.
  • Increased Mobility: Improves hip and shoulder joint mobility while absorbing impact that would otherwise stress your hips and knees.

  • Versatility: Adaptable to all fitness levels and ages, and excellent as a cross-training activity.

These combined benefits make Nordic Walking an enjoyable, effective, and sustainable way to stay active — perfect for everyone from beginners to seasoned athletes.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Brief History of Nordic Walking and Pole Differences
fields.body:
For decades during the 1900s, Finnish athletes trained for winter cross-country skiing by walking in the summer with ski poles — a practice they called “ski-walking.” This simple off-season training method later evolved into what we now know as Nordic Walking.

In 1966, Leena Jääskeläinen (born 1939), a gym teacher in Viherlaakso, Helsinki, Finland, began using “walking with ski poles” in physical education sessions for her students. Later, as a faculty member of the Physical Education Department at the University of Jyväskylä, she continued to promote this form of exercise. In 1987, she presented her ideas on exercise walking with poles publicly for the first time at the Finlandia Walk (“Finlandia kävely”) in Tampere, Finland. Her work caught the attention of the Finnish Central Association for Recreational Sports and Outdoor Activities, helping to popularize the concept nationally.

From Finland, Nordic Walking quickly spread to Sweden, Denmark, and throughout Europe, then to the USA and around the world. Today, it’s estimated that over 12 million Europeans practice Nordic Walking. The Helsinki-based International Nordic Walking Federation (inwa-nordicwalking.com) has conducted extensive research showing Nordic Walking’s positive health effects for people with arthritis, heart disease, diabetes, and other conditions.

What’s the Difference Between Nordic Walking and Ski Poles?

Although both types of poles assist in movement, they are designed for very different purposes:

  • Ski Poles: Intended for snow-based activities such as cross-country or downhill skiing. They are designed for propulsion on snow and vary depending on the skiing style.
  • Nordic Walking Poles: Specifically made for walking and hiking on various terrains — grass, dirt, sand, asphalt, or snow-free trails. They are shorter than ski poles and often come in one-piece or adjustable designs.
  • Materials: Common materials include aluminum, carbon fiber, or fiberglass for a lightweight yet durable build.
  • Support and Stability: Nordic Walking poles feature adjustable lengths, rubber tips for pavement, and carbide tips for off-road grip.
  • Grips: Ergonomically designed for walking, Nordic Walking grips are often cushioned and shaped for comfort and efficiency. They allow for a relaxed hand motion and effective use of straps.

In short, Nordic Walking poles are optimized for balance, comfort, and versatility across different terrains, while ski poles are specialized tools for snow-based propulsion and stability.

fields.title: About Nordic  Walking: Common Hazards of Nordic Walking
fields.body:
While Nordic Walking is a safe and enjoyable activity for most people, there are some potential hazards to be aware of. Understanding these risks can help you stay safe and get the most out of your walks.

  1. Uneven Terrain: Rough or uneven ground can increase the risk of tripping or stumbling. Stay alert and watch your footing.
  2. Weather Conditions: Rain, snow, or ice can make surfaces slippery. Choose appropriate footwear and be cautious in wet or cold conditions.
  3. Wildlife Encounters: In certain regions, encounters with wildlife can occur. Stay aware of your surroundings and follow local safety guidelines.
  4. Overexertion: Pushing yourself too hard can cause fatigue or injury. Listen to your body and take breaks when needed.
  5. Improper Equipment: Ill-fitting poles or unsuitable footwear can lead to discomfort, blisters, or joint strain. Always use properly adjusted poles and supportive shoes.
  6. Traffic Hazards: Walking near roads can expose you to vehicle traffic. Stay on sidewalks or designated walking paths whenever possible.
  7. Dehydration: Inadequate fluid intake may cause dehydration or heat-related issues. Carry water and stay hydrated throughout your walk.
  8. Lack of Sun Protection: Extended exposure to the sun without sunscreen, hats, or sunglasses can result in sunburn or heat exhaustion.
  9. Medical Conditions: Individuals with pre-existing health issues should monitor their condition and consult a healthcare provider before engaging in Nordic Walking.
  10. Tripping Over Poles: Beginners may occasionally trip on their own poles. Practice proper technique and maintain awareness of pole placement.
  11. Group Dynamics: During group walks, coordination and communication are key to avoiding collisions and ensuring a smooth, enjoyable experience.

By staying mindful of these potential hazards and taking simple precautions — such as wearing proper gear, staying hydrated, and walking at a comfortable pace — you can enjoy the many benefits of Nordic Walking safely and confidently.

fields.title: About Nordic Walking: Common Mistakes in Nordic Walking
fields.body:
Even though Nordic Walking is simple to learn, some common mistakes can limit its benefits or lead to discomfort. Here are the most frequent errors and tips on how to avoid them:

  1. Incorrect Leg and Arm Coordination: Moving the same arm and leg together instead of in opposition can disrupt your rhythm and balance.
  2. Uncoordinated Arm and Leg Movements: Ensure that your arm swing matches your stride naturally — opposite arm to opposite leg.
  3. Insufficient Arm Extension: Bending elbows too much or gripping the handle tightly prevents a full arm swing. Keep your arms relaxed and extend them naturally.
  4. Planting Poles Too Far Ahead: Poles should never go past your lead foot. Keep them angled backward for proper propulsion.
  5. No Arm Swing: A stiff or minimal arm swing reduces the workout’s effectiveness. Let your arms move freely and rhythmically.
  6. Tension in Neck and Shoulders: Holding too tightly or poor posture can create tension. Relax your shoulders and loosen your grip.
  7. Inability to Walk Faster: Overly tight or short movements limit your stride. Relax, extend your arms, and push off with purpose.
  8. Wrist Tension: Keeping wrists rigid prevents fluid motion. Let them move naturally with the pole swing.
  9. Head Down: Looking down constantly strains your neck and reduces balance. Keep your gaze forward and enjoy the scenery.
  10. Dragging Poles: Failing to lift poles properly can cause them to catch on the ground. Lift and plant them actively.
  11. Small Arm Swing and Steps: Tiny steps and short arm swings limit momentum. Use a full stride and natural arm motion.
  12. Incomplete Arm Swing: Not releasing the strap when the pole is behind your body restricts movement. Open your hand at the back of each swing.
  13. Incorrect Posture: Leaning too far forward or backward causes imbalance. Maintain a tall, upright position with relaxed shoulders.
  14. Gripping Handles Too Tightly: Over-gripping can cause forearm pain. Hold handles loosely, allowing space between your palm and the handle.
  15. Failure to Engage Core Muscles: Not activating your core reduces stability and power. Keep your abdominal muscles gently engaged.
  16. Inadequate Breathing: Shallow or irregular breathing can lead to fatigue. Practice deep, rhythmic breathing for endurance and relaxation.
  17. Lack of Posture Awareness: Forgetting about posture diminishes effectiveness. Stay upright, relaxed, and mindful throughout your walk.

By being aware of these common mistakes and practicing good technique, you can enjoy smoother, more efficient, and more rewarding Nordic Walking sessions.

fields.title: Important: What to Do If a Participant Feels Unwell
fields.body:
As an NWU event Organizer and Host, your first responsibility is the safety and wellbeing of your group. If a participant becomes unwell or there is a possible emergency during a walk, follow the steps below.

1. Stay Calm and Stop the Group

  • Stay calm - your calmness reassures everyone.
  • Stop the group in a safe location away from traffic, water edges, or hazards.

2. Check In With the Person

Approach gently and ask:

  • “How are you feeling?”
  • “Are you dizzy, cold, overheated, short of breath, or in pain?”

Observe for warning signs:

  • Pale, flushed, sweaty, shivering, or weak
  • Trouble speaking or confusion
  • Difficulty breathing
  • Chest pain, severe headache, fainting, or inability to stand/walk

If severe symptoms are present, treat it as an emergency and call your local emergency services immediately.

3. Decide: Rest, Turn Back, or Call Emergency Services

a) Mild symptoms

  • Move the person to a more comfortable environment (shade, shelter, or away from wind).
  • Adjust clothing: loosen layers in heat, add warmth in cold.
  • Offer small sips of water if they are fully awake and able to drink.
  • Encourage slow breathing and rest.

After resting, ask whether they want to:

  • Rest longer,
  • Walk back slowly, or
  • Continue only if fully recovered.

b) Symptoms do not improve

  • Do not leave the person alone.
  • End their participation for the day.
  • Ask a trusted participant to either lead the group back or stay with the group while you stay with the unwell person.
  • If in doubt, call local emergency services.

c) Call emergency services immediately if you notice:

  • Chest pain or severe difficulty breathing
  • Sudden confusion or inability to communicate
  • Weakness or numbness on one side of the body
  • Loss of consciousness or repeated fainting
  • Extremely hot or extremely cold body temperature
  • Seizures
  • Symptoms that rapidly worsen

When unsure - always choose to call for help.

4. While Waiting for Help

  • Stay with the person at all times.
  • Keep them warm or gently cool them depending on the situation.
  • Reassure them with a calm, steady voice.
  • Follow all instructions given by the emergency operator.
  • If appropriate, notify their emergency contact.

5. Managing the Rest of the Group

  • Explain calmly that someone is unwell and you are assisting them.
  • Ask a responsible participant to safely lead the group back if needed.
  • Never send the group back alone without a leader.
  • If safer, keep the entire group together until help arrives.

6. After the Incident

  • Record the date, time, location, and what you observed.
  • Document all actions you took.
  • Note whether emergency services were involved.
  • Notify NWU leadership through the CONTACT US tab.
  • Do not share medical details with the group or online.

7. Important Notes

  • NWU Organizers and Hosts are not expected to provide medical treatment.

  • Your responsibilities are:

    • Keep the group safe,
    • Stay with the unwell person,
    • Call local emergency services when needed,

    • Inform NWU afterward.

       

    By acting thoughtfully and responsibly, you help create a safe, caring, and trusted environment for everyone in the Nordic Walking United community.

    Thank you for leading with care, awareness, and heart. 🌿

fields.title: Find a Nordic Walk or Event on the Map
fields.body:
Welcome to the NWU Events Map!
Finding an event is easy and fun - just follow these simple steps:

  1. Open the Events Map
  2. Zoom in or out to find your desired location.
  3. Click on an event icon on the map
  4. Click the link that appears to view event details and register

How to Zoom In and Out on the NWU Events Map

The NWU Events Map lets you explore walks and activities around the world. You can zoom in or out easily using either a mouse or a touch screen.

Zooming with a Mouse (Desktop or Laptop)

  • Place your cursor anywhere on the Events map.
  • Scroll the mouse wheel forward (up) to zoom in and see events more closely.
  • Scroll the mouse wheel backward (down) to zoom out and view a wider area.
  • Keep scrolling gently until you find the level that feels just right.

Tip: You can also click and drag the map to move around once you’ve zoomed in.

Zooming with Fingers (Touch Screen)

  • Touch the Events map with two fingers.
  • Move your fingers apart (pinch out) to zoom in.
  • Move your fingers together (pinch in) to zoom out.
  • Adjust slowly until the map shows the area you’d like to explore.

Tip: Use one finger to drag the map and explore nearby locations.

That’s it!
Enjoy discovering Nordic Walks and events near you, across your region, and around the world. 🌍🌿

fields.body:
A blog is a wonderful way to stay connected with your local and global Nordic Walking United community. Through blog posts, you can:

  • 📸 Share photos from your events

  • 🚶 Tell the story of your walk

  • 💬 Share feedback, reflections, and highlights

  • 🌍 Inspire Nordic Walkers in other regions

  • ✨ And much more

Note: Only Event Organizers and Co-organizers can publish blog posts that are visible to the full NWU community.

How to Write a Blog Post

Quick Menu (click to jump):

  • Step 1: Log in to the Admin Panel

  • Step 2: Open the Blog Section

  • Step 3: Create Your Blog Post

  • Step 4: Publish Your Blog

  • Step 5: Manage Comments on Your Blog

  • Step 6: Delete Your Blog Post

Step 1: Log in to the Admin Panel

Click the Admin Panel link provided in your Approval email.

Log in using your email and password.

Step 2: Open the Blog Section

In the Admin Panel:

  • Go to Blog

  • Click on Posts

  • Click + Add or Add Post + 

    Click any image below to enlarge (opens in a new tab):

Step 3: Create Your Blog Post

Now the fun part! 🎉

  • Enter the Title of your blog post

  • Write your text in the editor

  • Add photos directly into the text if you wish

  • Use the editor tools to format your post and make it clear, welcoming, and beautiful

Click the link to view detailed Text Editor instructions (opens in a new tab): Using the Text Editor While Creating Events and Blogs 

Step 4: Publish Your Blog Post

When your post is ready:

  • ✅ Check the “Is published” checkbox

  • Click the SAVE button (see above)

🎉 Great job! Your blog post is now live and visible to the entire NWU community. You can see your blog on NWU website:

Step 5: Manage Comments on Your Blog

As a blog owner, you have full control over which comments appear on your website. To keep your blog welcoming, respectful, and aligned with your values, all comments must be approved in the Admin Panel before they are published.

Appropriate and thoughtful comments can be approved and shared.
If a comment is inappropriate, irrelevant, or spam, it should be deleted and will not appear on the website.

⚠️ Important
Any use or display of offensive, profane, or otherwise inappropriate language or images is strictly prohibited on the NWU website.

Access the Comments Section

  1. Click the Admin Panel link provided in your approval email.

  2. Log in using your email and password.

  3. Open Blog → Comments.

A) Approve Comment(s)

Option 1: Approve a Single Comment

  1. Click on a comment to open and read it.
  2. Check the “Is approved” checkbox.
  3. Click SAVE.

Once approved, the comment will appear on the website.

Option 2: Approve One or Multiple Comments

  1. Go to Admin Panel → Comments.
  2. Select one or more comments using the checkboxes.
  3. From the Action dropdown, choose “Approve selected comments”.
  4. Click Execute.

✅ You can approve multiple comments at the same time.

B) Delete Comment(s)

Option 1: Delete a Single Comment

  1. Open the comment.
  2. Review its content.
  3. Click the red “Delete” button.

  4. Confirm deletion.

Option 2: Delete One or Multiple Comments

  1. Go to Admin Panel → Comments.
  2. Select the comment(s) you want to delete.
  3. Choose “Delete selected comments” from the Action dropdown.
  4. Click Execute.

⚠️ Note: Deleted comments are permanently removed and will not appear on the website.

Step 6: Delete Your Blog Post

If you need to remove your blog post from the website, you can easily delete it from the Admin Panel. This action is helpful if a post is outdated, published by mistake, or no longer relevant.

How to Delete a Blog Post

  1. Log in to the Admin Panel.
  2. Open the Blog section.
  3. Click on Posts.
  4. Select the blog post(s) you want to delete by checking the checkbox next to each post.
  5. Click the Action dropdown list.
  6. Select “Delete selected posts”.
  7. Click the Execute button.

✅ You can delete one or multiple blog posts at the same time by selecting more than one checkbox.

⚠️ Note: Deleted blog posts are permanently removed and will no longer appear on the website.

 

✨Your blog is more than a post - it’s a shared footprint on our collective path. Each story, photo, and reflection helps weave our local walks into a global NWU journey, inspiring others to step outside, connect, and move with intention.

Thank you for being a voice of Nordic Walking United!

fields.title: Using the Text Editor When Creating Events and Blogs
fields.body:
Dear Nordic Walking Organizers & Hosts,

When you’re working in the Admin Panel, the text editor is your helper. It helps you format your text so your event descriptions and blog posts are clear, welcoming, and easy to read.

Below is a simple guide to the most useful tools you’ll use when creating events and sharing stories.

Bold Text

Use Bold to highlight important details such as:

  • meeting time
  • location
  • key instructions

How to use: Select the text → click B (Bold)

Example:

Meeting time: 9:00 AM

 

Italic Text

Use Italic to add gentle emphasis.

How to use: Select text → click I (Italic)

Example: Newcomers are welcome to walk at their own pace.

Underline

Use Underline sparingly to draw attention to key details.

How to use: Select text → click U (Underline)

Example: Please arrive 10 minutes early.

• Bullet List

Bullet lists make information easy to scan.

How to use: Click the Bullet List icon, then type items.

  • Warm-up exercises
  • Nordic walk
  • Cool-down stretching

1️⃣ Numbered List

Ideal for step-by-step instructions.

How to use: Click the Numbered List icon.

  1. Gentle warm-up
  2. Nordic walking practice

  3. Stretching and relaxation

🖼 Insert Image

Images help bring your events and blogs to life.

How to use: Click Insert Image → upload or select an image → adjust alignment.

Important: Images should be no more than 700 × 700 px. Larger images may take up too much space in the event description or blog section on the website.

 

🔠 Font Size

Adjust font size to improve readability.

How to use: Select text → choose a Font Size from the dropdown.

🔤 Font Type

Select a font type that looks clean and consistent.

How to use: Select text → choose a Font Type from the dropdown.

🎨 Font Color

Use sparingly to highlight important notes.

How to use: Select text → click Font Color → choose a color.

🖍 Font Background Color

Great for short reminders or special notices.

How to use: Select text → click Font Background Color → choose a color.

🌿 Best Practices

  • Keep your text clear, warm, and friendly.
  • Use formatting to support readability, not overwhelm.
  • Preview your post before publishing.

Well-formatted posts help participants feel informed, welcome, and confident.

    ▶ Watch on YouTube

Don’t try to be perfect right away. Nordic Walking is a practice. Watch one video, go for a short walk, and enjoy the process. Your rhythm will improve naturally with every step.

fields.title: FAQ
fields.body:
Nordic Walking United (NWU) is built on kindness, community, and the joy of moving together in nature.

This shared commitment helps ensure that NWU events remain welcoming, inclusive, and enjoyable for everyone, from first-time walkers to experienced hosts. Below are the most frequently asked questions from our organizers.

🌱 Organizer Basics

❓ How long should a Nordic Walking event be?

Most NWU walks are designed to be enjoyable and accessible for a wide range of people.

  • Typical walks last 30-90 minutes, including warm-up and cool-down.
  • Longer walks are welcome, as long as they match your group’s ability level.

❓ Do I need a sweep for every walk?

A sweep walks at the end of the group and helps keep everyone together.

  • Recommended for groups with more than 8 participants.
  • Optional for small groups, but always helpful and appreciated.

❓ What should I do if the weather is bad?

Safety always comes first. You may:

  • Cancel the event
  • Postpone it
  • Switch to a safer nearby route

🛡️ Safety, Respect & Photos

❓ What if someone doesn’t want to be in photos?

You must honor their request - always.

  • Even with signed consent, participants may opt out for a specific event.
  • Ask before the walk: "Does anyone prefer not to be in photos today?"
  • If someone objects, do not include them.
  • When unsure, always ask before posting photos.

❓ What should I do if someone gets injured or feels unwell?

  • Stop the group immediately.
  • Make sure the person is safe and supported.
  • Seek medical help if needed.
  • Stay calm and follow common-sense safety steps.

❓ What if a participant behaves disrespectfully?

You may:

  • Give a calm verbal reminder or warning
  • Document the incident
  • Report it to NWU via CONTACT US

If safety is threatened, you may ask the person to leave the event.

🌿 Group Dynamics & Growth

❓ How do I handle slow walkers or mixed ability levels?

The goal is for everyone to feel welcome and supported.

  • Keep the pace conversational.
  • Ask faster walkers to regroup regularly.
  • Use a sweep to support slower walkers.
  • Choose routes with natural regroup points.

❓ How do I grow my walking group?

Small, consistent actions make a big difference:

  • Post friendly follow-up summaries.
  • Share photos (with consent).
  • Engage warmly in comments.
  • Encourage participants to invite friends.
  • Be consistent: warmth + reliability = growth.

💚 Policies & Follow-Ups

❓ Can I charge a fee for my event?

Donations are allowed only if they are clearly stated as optional.

❓ What should my follow-up message look like?

A good follow-up message can:

  • Thank participants
  • Share a warm event summary
  • Include photos (with permission)
  • Mention the next upcoming walk

🤝 Help & Support

❓ What if I need help or advice?

Organizers are never alone.

  • Contact NWU leadership anytime via CONTACT US.
  • We’re happy to help with safety, planning, group dynamics, and more.
  • If you’re unsure how to handle a situation, reach out - we’re here to support you!

fields.title: Nordic Walk in Bare Cove Magicland! Feb.7, 2026
author: yanandksusha@yahoo.com
fields.body:
Dear Nordic Walkers and Friends ☀️,

I am happy to share with you that we had a magical Nordic Walk  today in snow-covered Bare Cove.

Everything felt just right: soft snow falling from the sky, the frozen river quietly resting beside us, and that beautiful crunch of snow under our feet. There were only a couple of dog walkers, otherwise, it felt like the whole park belonged just to us.

At the end, we warmed up with Ksenya’s NWU Rejuvenating Herbal Tea, brewed with love and care ☕
The tea included a nourishing mix of healthful herbs and local treasures: German chamomile from my garden, local cranberries from Hanson, local pollen from Pembroke, turmeric with black and cayenne pepper, and a couple of teaspoons of an herbal blend from Latvia, including yarrow (Achillea millefolium), wonderful for digestion. I also added a handful of blackberries and — just to make the day more interesting — a handful of fresh kale 😉

Thank you to everyone who wasn’t scared of the blizzard - you are brave, resilient, and wonderful.
Keep smiling, breathing, and walking, team.
See you soon,

Ksenya
